verdicts.reason: Quote is the framing paragraph at lines 3-4 verbatim (line wrap joined with a space). The statement adds nothing beyond it: the subject (pagination of the address book's lists and the party pickers) and the trigger (the manage-notifications pre-flight, registering ruling:paul-2026-11-05 against ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 over req-611) are both in the quote. Provenance rather than a decision, as its note says.

"Pagination should be kept. We want it." is on line 6, inside the owner's block quote. The statement restates exactly that. ref says lines 6-7 where the words sit on line 6 alone; a loose ref does not spoil the claim.
"It was removed previously in error." is on line 6 of the owner's block quote, and the statement is a direct restatement.

Quote spans lines 6-7 of the block quote verbatim ("We actually fixed that theme removing it with a bug EUDPA-827"). The owner's wording is clumsy, but the reading that the theme which removed pagination has been fixed by bug EUDPA-827 is the only available one, and decided point 4 (lines 47-49) confirms EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed.

Quote is the first "What was asked" bullet, lines 13-15, verbatim. The statement frames it as one of the two opposed readings put to the owner, which lines 11-18 support, and its note correctly flags that this is the question, not the decision.

Quote is the second "What was asked" bullet, lines 16-18, verbatim, including the nested quotation of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6. The statement restates it without overreach and the note flags it as the question, superseded by decided point 2.

"**Pagination is kept, and its removal was an error.** Every address book list and every address picker pages." is decided point 1, line 22. The statement takes only the second sentence, which the quote carries verbatim.
Decided point 1, lines 22-23: "No requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated." Quoted verbatim across the line wrap and restated exactly.
Decided point 2's bold heading, lines 25-26, says req-611's 'unpaginated' clause is dropped. Quote verbatim, statement is its first half.

Same quote at lines 25-26 carries "and `ruling:ian-2026-11-23` point 6 is superseded on that point alone". The statement reads "that point" as the req-611 'unpaginated' point, which is what the heading's first half names and what the framing paragraph (lines 3-4) says the conflict was over. Note correctly ties it to the named conflict.

Lines 26-27 verbatim: "Its reasoning rested on a premise that is no longer true of the service: the address book's list endpoint does take roles, and it does page." The statement reorders but adds nothing.

First code-citation bullet of decided point 2, lines 29-30, verbatim. The statement names the same four filters (searchTerm, countryCodes, roles, searchRoles) as a list request's filters. A claim about what the service's code does today, reported by the ruling, not a decision of the ruling.
Second code-citation bullet, lines 31-32, quotes AddressController's own words: the list "Lists the caller's live addresses, newest first, one page at a time". The statement restates exactly that.
"`page` 1-based defaulting to 1" is on line 32, in the AddressController bullet. Statement matches.

Lines 32-34 verbatim: "`pageSize` running from `ListPaging.MIN_PAGE_SIZE` to `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` defaulting to `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`". Statement matches, naming the constants rather than resolving them (claim p1-017 carries the resolved 1 to 100, default 25).

"taking `roles` and `searchRoles` alongside them." is on lines 33-34. "them" in the bullet is page and pageSize, which the statement spells out: a sound reading of the sentence it closes, not an overreach.

Third code-citation bullet, lines 35-36, verbatim: ListPaging.java is "1 to 100, default 25, exactly the bounds `ruling:paul-2026-11-05` point 8 names". The statement attributes those bounds to the list page size, which is what the bullet's constants (MIN/MAX/DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE, line 33) are. Holds.

Line 38 verbatim: "The role filter therefore runs in the service, before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong." The statement spells out "it" as the role filter, which the sentence's subject makes plain.
Line 39 verbatim: "\"The list endpoint takes no role\" described an earlier address book, not the one on `main`." Statement is identical.
Lines 39-40 verbatim: "Paul's point 8 stands in full and is the position to distil." Statement names Paul's point 8 as ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8, which lines 13-15 and 36 establish.
Decided point 3's bold heading, line 42: "**The rest of `ruling:ian-2026-11-23` stands.**" Statement matches.
"The party pickers page at eight" is on line 42, immediately after point 3's heading. Statement matches verbatim.
Lines 42-43 verbatim: "the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s acceptance criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped". Statement matches.
"`req-594` and `req-595` stay dropped" is on line 43. Statement matches.
Lines 43-44 verbatim: "the \"Selected address\" restatement comes back with the paging." Statement matches; kind "copy" is apt for a restatement of wording.

Lines 44-45 verbatim: "That ruling and this one agree that pages are paged; they differed only on whether the address book's own list API was one of them." The statement resolves "That ruling" as ruling:ian-2026-11-23, which point 3's heading on line 42 names.

Decided point 4, lines 47-49, verbatim, including the commit 0d1d606d, its message and the merge to main on 24 November. The statement's gloss "the fix for the removed pagination" follows from the owner's block quote (line 6-7) tying EUDPA-827 to the removal, so it is not an overreach.
Line 49 verbatim: "with this workspace's `1ec8d9b7` for the behaviour spec." Statement matches.
Line 49 verbatim: "The live animals pickers need no further work." Statement is identical.
Decided point 5's bold heading, line 51, verbatim: conflict c-292 is settled and the plants contact picker keeps its pagination. Note correctly records that it answers c-292.
Lines 51-53 verbatim. The statement spells out "that picker" as the plants contact picker, which the heading on line 51 names, and records what c-292 asked rather than a decision, as its note says.

"Nothing drops either, so it keeps both" is on line 53; "either"/"both" refer to the five-a-page pagination and the 'Selected address' inset named on line 52, which the statement spells out. Sound, not an overreach.

Lines 53-54 verbatim: "and takes the shared layout change (`req-1964`) as its default already said." Statement matches, with the subject (the plants contact picker) taken from the same sentence's "it".

Decided point 6, line 56: "**The plants contact picker pages at eight**, not five". Verbatim, and the statement says only that. Recorded as a decision rather than an open point, which is right: the point carries Ian's own confirmation on line 62.

Lines 56-59 verbatim, including both citations (insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49 and REQ-INS-ADDR-013) and the reference to ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1. Statement adds nothing the quote does not carry.

Quote joins lines 59-60 and the block quote on line 62 verbatim (blank line between kept as \n\n). The statement is supported: the page size was asked as an orchestrator's call because point 5 settles only that the picker pages, and "contact picker should be 8 yes" is Ian's confirmation the same day. The note's reading, that the confirmation turns it from an open point into a decision, is sound.
Line 64 verbatim: "Five-in-one-picker against eight-in-the-rest was a difference nothing recorded a reason for." Statement restates it.

The source is not silent where this gap says it is. Decided point 6, lines 56-58, says every picker pages "at the one figure the INS address book list already uses", and point 6's figure is eight (line 56), so the ruling does state the page size of an address book list: the INS address book list already shows eight, cited to insfrontend:.../list/list.controller.js:49 and REQ-INS-ADDR-013. The statement's "it names eight only for the pickers" is therefore contradicted by the text it refs. Recorded instead as missed claim ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-035-m1.

Looked at decided point 2 (lines 25-27) and point 1 (lines 22-23): the ruling drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and says no requirement says a list is served or shown unpaginated, but nowhere states what req-611 requires in its place, or whether anything of req-611 survives. The source is indeed silent, so the gap holds.

Lines 16-18 record the premise (a caller reads the list and filters by role itself) and lines 26-27 and 38 set it aside for the service, but the ruling says nothing anywhere about changing a consumer that reads the whole list today to page the API instead. Silent where the gap says, so it holds.

Point 4 (line 49) closes out the live animals pickers and point 6 changes the plants contact picker's page size, but across lines 47-64 the ruling never says whether any other place pagination was removed from still needs work — the plants consignor and place of destination pickers of point 5's framing are named only as what inc-087 dropped. The silence is real, so the gap holds.

missed.statement: The INS address book list already pages at eight: point 6 sets the plants contact picker at eight precisely so every picker pages at "the one figure the INS address book list already uses", so that figure is eight.
missed.quote: **The plants contact picker pages at eight**, not five, so every picker in both journeys pages at the one figure the INS address book list already uses (`insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49`, `REQ-INS-ADDR-013`)
missed.note: No claim in the extract records the address book list's own page size; p1-035 records only that the pickers match it, and p1-038 wrongly treats it as a gap. The citations insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49 and REQ-INS-ADDR-013 are where the figure is already implemented, so this is existing behaviour the ruling confirms rather than a change it makes.
